source: AI text detectors generally exploit statistical regularities in common model outputs rather than an intrinsic signature of machine authorship. Those regularities can arise from post-training, decoding choices, and standardized assistant behavior. As language models improve at reproducing the distribution of human writing, purely text-based detection should become less reliable in principle.

These patterns often develop through post-training training, during decoding choices, and the standardized behavior of standardized assistants. As language models enhance their ability to reproduce the distribution of human writing, purely text-based detection will increasingly become less reliable in practice.
